title: Chapter 2 Mastery Quiz: The Birth of Experimental Psychology & Structuralism
description: Demonstrate comprehensive mastery of Wundt's Leipzig lab, introspection, voluntarism, and Titchener's Structuralism.

questions.question: Which historic event marks the formal establishment of psychology as an independent academic science?

options.text: The publication of Darwin's 'Origin of Species'
Wilhelm Wundt founding his Leipzig laboratory in 1879

questions.explanation: Wilhelm Wundt establishing his formal laboratory at the University of Leipzig in 1879 is recognized as psychology's founding event.

questions.question: What title was given to Wilhelm Wundt's 1874 textbook that explicitly proposed psychology as an experimental discipline?
questions.explanation: Wundt's 1874 text 'Principles of Physiological Psychology' established experimental methods as central to psychology.

questions.question: What name did Wilhelm Wundt give to his own theoretical approach to psychology?
questions.explanation: Wundt termed his psychology 'Voluntarism' because he emphasized the active power of the human will in organizing consciousness.

questions.question: In Wundt's theory, how does 'apperception' differ from passive 'perception'?

options.text: Apperception is unconscious, whereas perception is conscious
Apperception is the active, voluntary focusing of attention to synthesize mental content
Apperception occurs only in non-human animals
Apperception is a reflex without brain involvement

questions.explanation: Wundt defined apperception as the active, intentional focus of attention that organizes sensory contents into unified wholes.

questions.question: What was the subject matter of Wundt's massive 10-volume work entitled 'Völkerpsychologie'?

options.text: Reaction time measurements of Leipzig students
Higher mental processes studied through language, myth, customs, and culture

questions.explanation: 'Völkerpsychologie' explored higher mental processes through the historical study of language, folklore, religion, and culture.

questions.question: In Wundt's laboratory, how was experimental introspection (Selbstbeobachtung) controlled?

options.text: Subjects freely described whatever childhood memories came to mind
Trained observers gave immediate reports under strictly repeated and varied physical stimulus conditions
Subjects were placed under deep hypnotic trances
Observers were never allowed to practice beforehand

questions.explanation: Wundt enforced strict experimental controls: trained observers, immediate reporting, and systematic stimulus repetition.

questions.question: Which of the following represents the three dimensions of feeling in Wundt's Tridimensional Theory?
questions.explanation: Wundt's three affective dimensions were Lust/Unlust (Pleasure/Displeasure), Spannung/Lösung (Tension/Relaxation), and Erregung/Beruhigung (Excitement/Calm).

questions.question: Which student of Wundt brought experimental psychology to Cornell University and founded Structuralism?
questions.explanation: Edward Bradford Titchener established the Structuralist school of psychology at Cornell University in Ithaca, New York.

questions.question: What did Titchener define as the 'Stimulus Error'?

options.text: Failing to present a loud enough acoustic click
Confusing the physical object or its meaning with the raw conscious sensory experience
Allowing the subject to fall asleep during testing
Mistaking an unconditioned response for a conditioned response

questions.explanation: The stimulus error occurs when observers name the object itself (e.g. 'table') rather than reporting elemental sensations (color, texture, brightness).

questions.question: Approximately how many individual elemental sensations did Titchener and his students catalog?
questions.explanation: Titchener identified more than 44,000 individual conscious sensory qualities, of which over 32,000 were visual.

questions.question: What was the fundamental theoretical difference between Wundt's Voluntarism and Titchener's Structuralism?

options.text: Wundt emphasized active attention and synthesis; Titchener sought passive atomic elements
Wundt studied animal reflexes; Titchener studied human dreams
Wundt rejected introspection; Titchener invented it
Titchener studied culture; Wundt only studied vision

questions.explanation: Wundt viewed the mind as actively synthesizing experience through apperception, whereas Titchener reduced consciousness to passive sensory elements.

questions.question: What controversy arose between Titchener and Oswald Külpe's Würzburg school regarding introspection?

options.text: Whether 'imageless thought' can exist without sensory elements
Whether IQ tests are culturally biased

questions.explanation: Külpe's lab found that thoughts can occur without sensory images ('imageless thought'), which contradicted Titchener's fundamental assertion.

questions.question: Why could Structuralism NOT address questions regarding child development or animal psychology?

options.text: Children and animals could not provide trained introspective verbal reports
Titchener believed children had no brain
Federal laws banned testing animals in universities
Cornell University did not permit animals on campus

questions.explanation: Because Structuralism relied strictly on trained verbal introspection, infants, children, and animals were methodologically excluded.

questions.question: What term describes the problem where the very process of observing one's conscious state alters the experience being observed?
questions.explanation: Introspective observation inherently interferes with the phenomenon being observed, such as cooling off spontaneous anger when attempting to analyze it.

questions.question: Which apparatus was commonly used in Wundt's lab to record reaction times to millisecond accuracy?
questions.explanation: The Hipp chronoscope was the classic precision brass instrument in early experimental laboratories used to measure reaction times in thousandths of a second.

questions.question: What was the American psychological establishment's chief criticism of Structuralism in the early 20th century?

options.text: It was too applied and commercialized
It was sterile, impractical, and ignored how mind helps humans adapt
It used too many mathematical formulas
It focused excessively on social groups

questions.explanation: American psychologists influenced by evolutionary theory found Structuralism sterile and divorced from practical adaptation and living.

questions.question: What happened to the school of Structuralism after Edward Titchener passed away in 1927?

options.text: It grew to dominate all modern cognitive science
It largely vanished as an active school, superseded by Functionalism and Behaviorism

questions.explanation: Structuralism essentially died with Titchener, as newer movements like Functionalism, Gestalt, and Behaviorism displaced it.

questions.question: What was Structuralism's greatest positive contribution to modern psychology?

options.text: Its 44,000 elements are still memorized by all medical students
It established psychology as an empirical laboratory science committed to experimental rigor
It created the first standard intelligence test

questions.explanation: Structuralism firmly embedded psychology within laboratory science, establishing experimental discipline, instrumentation, and empirical standards.

questions.question: Titchener formed an exclusive all-male dining and discussion group in 1904 known as what?
questions.explanation: Titchener founded 'The Experimentalists' in 1904, deliberately excluding women until after his death, when it was reorganized as the Society of Experimental Psychologists.

questions.question: Which female psychologist was Edward Titchener's very first doctoral student at Cornell, earning the first PhD in psychology awarded to an American woman in 1894?
questions.explanation: Margaret Floy Washburn was Titchener's first graduate student, becoming the first American woman to officially receive a PhD in psychology in 1894.

questions.question: What is 'creative synthesis' in Wundt's voluntaristic psychology?

options.text: The emergence of new mental properties through apperception that cannot be explained simply by summing elements
The biological creation of new neurons in the cortex
The artistic imagination required to compose poetry
The fabrication of false memories under hypnosis

questions.explanation: Wundt's creative synthesis stated that apperception combines sensory elements into complex psychic compounds with emergent qualities not found in isolated elements.

questions.question: Why did Gestalt psychologists subsequently attack both Wundt and Titchener?

options.text: Because both treated consciousness as an artificial collection of isolated building blocks or 'elements'
Because they refused to study optical illusions

questions.explanation: Gestalt psychologists rejected 'elementalism' (or 'brick-and-mortar psychology'), insisting that experience is inherently holistic and cannot be dissected into atoms.
